nodes.details: Exposed HTTP handlers for configuration validation that return error messages directly to the client.
The plugin processes configuration inputs and returns error messages without prior neutralization of special characters.

nodes.summary: missing html escaping in error output
nodes.details: Error messages generated during validation are rendered as raw HTML in the response, allowing injection of malicious markup.
The update modifies validation logic to strip or escape HTML tags from error messages before returning them to prevent injection.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation: 'Cross-site Scripting' ('XSS')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the console printer processes string objects containing newline characters.
An attacker can provide a string with an excessive number of newline characters to the printing function.
The implementation splits the input string by newlines without a limit, causing the resulting array to consume excessive memory and trigger an out-of-memory error.
The patch modifies the string splitting logic to accept a maximum row count parameter, preventing unbounded memory allocation and handling truncation gracefully.
The vulnerability is triggered when the web administration password is passed as a command-line argument to the server's main execution method.
The server must be launched via the command line interface with the password flag to expose the cleartext value in the system process list.
The argument validation logic previously permitted the password flag to be processed directly from the command line, allowing the plaintext value to be exposed to local users.
The patch introduces a conditional check to reject the password argument when invoked from the command line, and modifies the password setter to only accept pre-hashed values.
The method functions as a configuration testing interface that validates external service connectivity using provided parameters.
The validation routine executed without verifying user privileges, permitting low-privilege accounts to trigger external network requests.
The lack of HTTP method constraints and authorization checks allowed credential harvesting and cross-site request forgery attacks.
The update mandates POST requests and implements conditional permission verification for both global and project-level configurations.
This method serves as the entry point for modifying parser settings, which can be exploited to trigger the vulnerability.
The vulnerability requires invoking the feature configuration method to alter the external entity processing setting.
Modifying the external entity feature does not update the internal entity expansion flag, allowing uncontrolled external entity processing.
The patch automatically updates the internal entity expansion flag whenever the external entity feature is modified to maintain consistency.

nodes.details: This method generates output filenames by concatenating base strings with user-provided application parameters.
The vulnerability requires an attacker possessing Item or Configure permission to supply malicious values for pipeline parameters.
The function directly incorporates unvalidated user input into a filename string without applying any security checks or encoding.
The patch introduces a sanitization step that applies raw encoding to the constructed filename before returning it for file operations.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The component processes HTTP requests to retrieve and serve file attachments based on user-provided parameters.
The application directly incorporates an unvalidated request parameter into a file system path construction operation.
Lack of validation on the input allows traversal sequences to escape the intended directory and access arbitrary system files.
The patch introduces a safe utility method to sanitize the user input before it is used to build the target file path.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when an agent process initiates a remote file read operation targeting the Jenkins controller.
Exploitation requires running Jenkins 2.318 or earlier, or LTS 2.303.2 or earlier, where the remote execution mechanism lacks adequate security controls.
The implementation uses a remote callable mechanism to read files on the controller without validating the target path or enforcing access restrictions.
The patch removes the remote callable execution and replaces it with a direct local file read operation, eliminating the attack surface for agent-driven controller file access.
The vulnerability is triggered through the system user recycle bin endpoint, which invokes logical deletion and restoration methods for user accounts.
The application accepts a list of user identifiers to perform batch logical deletion or restoration operations.
User identifiers are manually concatenated into a quoted, comma-separated string and passed directly to the data mapper, allowing malicious input to alter the intended SQL query structure.
The patch removes manual string formatting and passes the user identifier list directly to the mapper, enabling the underlying framework to safely parameterize the SQL statement.
The vulnerability is triggered when the plugin processes a message sent from an agent to the Jenkins controller.
An attacker must be able to control or compromise an agent process to send malicious requests to the controller.
The plugin creates a user-specified directory on the controller and parses files within it as test results without proper validation.
The fix updates the parameter annotation to enforce proper nullability constraints and changes the message direction to controller-to-agent, preventing untrusted controller-side execution.
This method processes test report output text and applies transformations before rendering it in the user interface.
The vulnerability requires an attacker possessing Item or Configure permission to inject malicious content into test report outputs that will be processed by the annotate method.
The method applies a regular expression to automatically wrap detected HTTP URLs in anchor tags without validating the content, enabling stored cross-site scripting when the output is rendered.
The patch eliminates the regular expression replacement that converts URLs to clickable links, ensuring only basic HTML entity escaping is applied to prevent script injection.
The vulnerability is triggered when a pipeline author specifies a file parameter for a pipeline input step, causing the plugin to process and archive the file on the controller.
The pipeline must be configured to allow unsafe parameters, or the plugin version must not yet enforce the prohibition of file parameters in input steps.
The plugin copies uploaded file parameters to the controller workspace using the parameter name directly as a relative path without sanitization, enabling arbitrary file system writes.
The patch introduces checks to detect and abort execution when file parameters are used, either by warning and allowing via a flag or by throwing an abort exception to prevent unsafe file archiving.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

nodes.details: Multiple storage backend methods construct filesystem paths using user-supplied container and key parameters without prior validation.
The storage backend accepts client-provided keys that are directly concatenated with a base directory path to locate files.
The implementation fails to sanitize or verify user-supplied path components, allowing directory traversal sequences to escape the intended storage root.
The patch normalizes constructed paths and invokes a validation routine to ensure all resolved locations remain strictly within the designated container directory.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The function processes external parameters to construct dynamic SQL query clauses.
The function accepts external parameters without prior validation or sanitization before query construction.
User-controlled values are directly interpolated into SQL strings using format operations, allowing malicious payloads to alter query logic.
The patch applies SQL escaping functions to string parameters and enforces integer parsing for identifier arrays to neutralize injection vectors.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

nodes.details: The HTTP endpoint responsible for processing requests to remove support bundle files from the controller.
The handler directly consumes bundle names from user-submitted form data without verifying their existence or safety.
Failure to validate submitted filenames against existing directory contents allows arbitrary file deletion on the controller filesystem.
The patch restricts deletion operations to only verify against a list of existing valid bundles before processing the request.

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when a user initiates a change request to edit a wiki document, which subsequently exports the modifications to an XML file.
The system permits editing any page by default through change requests and automatically exports the changes to a downloadable XML format accessible to any user.
The document preparation handler fails to validate whether the target document contains sensitive fields like passwords before allowing edits, enabling data exfiltration via XML export.
The patch adds a rights verification step to deny users the ability to edit documents containing password fields through change requests, thereby blocking sensitive data export.
The vulnerability originates from how TLS settings are managed at the plugin level rather than per domain.
The Jenkins Active Directory plugin is configured to use StartTLS for secure LDAP connections.
The plugin previously used a global TLS configuration or defaulted to trusting all certificates, bypassing proper certificate validation for domain connections.
The patch moves TLS configuration from the global realm to individual domain objects and explicitly passes domain-specific TLS settings to all LDAP bind operations.
The checkVncServ method serves as the form validation endpoint that processes user input and generates an HTML response.
The endpoint accepts a user-supplied parameter value and directly incorporates it into the response without prior sanitization.
The parameter value is concatenated directly into HTML markup without escaping, enabling reflected cross-site scripting attacks.
The patch modifies the response generation to apply an XML escaping function to the parameter value before embedding it in the HTML output.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the application processes XML documents using SAX or DOM parsers.
The application parses XML files such as configurations or POMs without enforcing restrictions on external resource resolution.
The underlying XML parser is not configured to block or limit the loading of external DTDs and entity references, allowing arbitrary network access.
The patch configures the parser factory and reader to restrict external schema and DTD access by default, introducing a policy to control external resource loading.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: This routine manages the lifecycle and generation of temporary files for system recording operations.
The method executes without explicit security manager privileges, leaving file operations exposed to standard access controls and potential race conditions.
Standard temporary file creation APIs are utilized without atomic operations or secure permissions, enabling manipulation through race conditions.
The update encapsulates the file operations within a privileged action to enforce secure execution and bypass restrictive security manager checks.
The vulnerability is triggered when the server processes client-supplied terminal dimension parameters via the negotiation protocol.
An attacker must establish a network connection to the telnet service and transmit dimension packets without requiring prior authentication.
The geometry configuration function only enforces minimum dimension thresholds, allowing maximum integer values that trigger continuous resource-intensive rendering cycles.
The patch adds upper bound comparisons against predefined maximum constants to clamp excessively large dimension values before processing.
The vulnerability is triggered when the parser is instantiated and begins processing input streams or readers.
The parser configuration lacks a predefined maximum depth setting, allowing arbitrarily deep JSON structures to be processed.
The internal context stack does not check its size before pushing new elements, leading to memory exhaustion on deeply nested inputs.
The update initializes the stack with a configurable depth limit and adds a size check during context pushes to reject overly nested documents.
This component manages the determination of the target URL following successful user authentication, which serves as the execution point for the redirect logic.
The authentication success handler accepts and processes a target URL from the session or request without verifying its legitimacy or origin.
The method directly returns the resolved target URL for redirection without checking if it points to a safe or internal destination, enabling external phishing redirects.
The patch introduces a validation step to verify the target URL safety before redirection, falling back to a default URL if the check fails.
The deprecated getName method serves as the entrypoint for exposing API key credentials to external components.
The system relies on a deprecated Principal implementation method that directly exposes the full API key without sanitization.
The method returns the complete API key string directly, enabling unauthorized access filters to bypass security controls using the exposed credential.
The patch modifies the retrieval method to truncate the credential, returning only the initial and final character segments separated by asterisks.
These methods function as HTTP endpoints that handle Active Directory connection validation and authentication testing for administrative users.
The endpoints previously accepted GET requests, allowing external parties to trigger sensitive administrative tests without explicit user intent or browser context.
The absence of a POST-only requirement on these endpoints permits cross-site request forgery attacks that can execute unauthorized connection and authentication tests.
The patch introduces the @RequirePOST annotation to both methods, ensuring they only process POST requests and effectively blocking CSRF exploitation vectors.
Pipelines can load arbitrary Groovy source files from the classpath to execute code without sandbox restrictions.
The plugin allows pipelines to load any Groovy source file bundled with Jenkins core or plugins.
The secure class loader creation lacks an allowlist mechanism, permitting execution of arbitrary Groovy source files.
The patch wraps the secure class loader with a custom implementation that enforces an allowlist of permitted Groovy source files.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

nodes.details: Triggered when JVM configurations disable Unsafe access, forcing a fallback path that ignores buffer indices.
When Unsafe access is restricted or unavailable, Netty returns pooled direct buffers that lack exposed memory addresses.
The fallback address calculation uses a zero-based offset, ignoring the buffer's current reader or writer index during cryptographic operations.
The patch introduces dedicated methods to correctly incorporate the buffer's reader and writer indices into the native memory address calculation.
This component handles the initialization of transformation contexts when parsing macro content, serving as the execution boundary for nested macros.
The vulnerability manifests when the transformation context operates in a restricted state, which is designed to block execution of privileged macros.
The parser incorrectly instantiates a new transformation context without inheriting the restricted flag from the parent context, effectively bypassing security restrictions.
The patch modifies the context initialization logic to explicitly query the parent context's restricted status and pass it to the new context constructor.
The vulnerability is triggered during the SAML authentication flow when handling the RelayState parameter in the login success callback.
The application accepts a RelayState value from the SAML response without sufficient validation before embedding it into a client-side script.

The original implementation used HTML entity escaping for the RelayState, which is insufficient for safely embedding untrusted data within a JavaScript string context, allowing XSS payloads to execute.
The patch replaces HTML escaping with UTF-8 URL encoding to properly sanitize the RelayState before injecting it into the redirection script, preventing script injection.
This method serves as the initial trigger where user-provided macro content is processed and potentially evaluated in an unintended context.
The macro processes its content using a separate transformation context, which allows nested macros to be evaluated outside their intended scope.
The original implementation deferred content parsing to a secondary macro, causing the footnote text to be executed in an isolated context rather than the original document context.
The patch modifies the macro to directly parse and return the content children within the current execution context, ensuring consistent evaluation and preventing unintended context switching.
The application extracts and decodes an XML stream from a PDF document, passing the raw content directly to an XML parser for validation.
The system processes XML data derived directly from an untrusted PDF file without implementing input validation or sanitization prior to parsing.
The code utilizes a default document builder factory without disabling external entity resolution or DOCTYPE declarations, allowing malicious XML structures to be processed.
The patch replaces the default factory instantiation with a dedicated secure builder method that enforces strict parsing constraints and disables dangerous features.
The HTTP endpoint populates a credential ID list for UI dropdowns, directly exposing stored credential identifiers to callers.
Attackers possessing only Overall/Read permissions can trigger the endpoint without requiring elevated administrative privileges.
The endpoint implementation omits any permission verification before returning sensitive credential identifiers, enabling unauthorized enumeration.
The patch inserts a mandatory administrative permission check at the method entry to restrict access to authorized users only.
The method processes input strings using regex pattern matching to perform replacements, serving as the direct execution path for the vulnerability.
The system processes external or untrusted strings through regex matching without implementing execution timeouts or interruption mechanisms.
Unoptimized regex patterns applied to untrusted input strings cause catastrophic backtracking, consuming excessive CPU resources and enabling denial of service.
The patch wraps the input string in a secure character sequence that tracks match operations, enabling the regex engine to be interrupted before exhausting system resources.
The plugin exposes credentials as environment variables but fails to handle special characters, allowing transformed values to bypass log masking.
The vulnerability requires stored secrets to contain dollar sign characters, which the build system interprets as escape sequences during environment variable resolution.
Raw credential values are directly injected into the build environment map without sanitization, allowing the build system to alter their content.
The patch iterates through credential values and replaces dollar signs with escaped sequences to prevent unintended transformation by the build system.
The constructor accepts a link parameter that is directly embedded into an HTML event handler attribute for build status badges.
The plugin accepts a link query parameter for badges without validating its protocol or restricting allowed values.
The link value is concatenated into an HTML attribute with inadequate escaping, allowing reflected cross-site scripting.
The patch restricts links to http and https protocols, applies double HTML escaping, and uses safe attribute quoting to prevent injection.

nodes.details: Handles form binding and initialization when users upload secret files through the Jenkins interface.
The system attempts to decrypt uploaded file contents to verify if they conform to an encrypted secret format.
When validation succeeds, the plugin incorrectly stores the file content unencrypted and only Base64 encoded on the controller filesystem.
The patch replaces the decryption method with a raw byte conversion to bypass content validation during credential creation.
The doValidate method acts as a form validation endpoint that processes user-supplied endpoint parameters.
Users with only Overall or Read permissions can access this endpoint and trigger external network requests.
The validation method fails to verify user privileges before executing the discovery process, enabling unauthorized external connections.
The update adds an administrative permission check to restrict the validation functionality to authorized personnel only.
Multiple Stapler-based HTTP endpoints in the plugin are exposed to external requests without adequate safeguards.
Attackers possessing only Overall or Read permissions can interact with the vulnerable endpoints to trigger unauthorized operations.
The affected endpoints fail to verify user permissions and do not enforce specific HTTP methods, enabling cross-site request forgery and unauthorized credential access.
The update mandates POST request methods and inserts explicit permission verification logic to restrict access to authorized administrators only.
The vulnerability is triggered when the pipeline utility step processes configuration files and applies variable interpolation.
The bundled configuration library enables dangerous prefix interpolators by default without administrator restriction.
The interpolation mechanism fails to validate or limit allowed prefix types, permitting arbitrary file system reads through specific protocol prefixes.
The patch explicitly configures the interpolation engine with a predefined whitelist of safe prefix lookups, blocking unauthorized file access.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

nodes.details: The configuration validation routine processes HTTP requests to verify cloud and agent template settings.
The endpoint is accessible to users with only read-level permissions, allowing them to trigger validation routines.
The validation routine executes without verifying caller privileges, exposing internal configuration details to low-privilege requests.
The patch enforces administrative permission checks and restricts the endpoint to POST requests to prevent unauthorized access.
The plugin allows configuring custom classpaths and database drivers through job settings, which are dynamically loaded at runtime.
An attacker must have permission to configure Jenkins jobs to supply malicious classpath or driver parameters.
The original implementation dynamically loads database drivers and resources using the thread's context classloader and user-controlled classpaths, allowing arbitrary class execution.
The patch introduces a dedicated classloader for the plugin and explicitly passes it to driver registration and resource accessors, eliminating reliance on the thread's context classloader.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the utility class attempts to generate and sign JSON Web Tokens for authentication purposes.
The cryptographic key for token signing is initialized as a static variable that defaults to a hardcoded value if not explicitly configured by the developer.
The application relies on a static, hardcoded secret key for HMAC-based token generation, enabling potential token forgery by unauthorized parties.
The patch adds a state flag to track custom key assignment and blocks token issuance by throwing an exception if the default hardcoded key remains active.
The HTTP POST endpoint handling expression previewing lacks security controls, allowing unverified requests to trigger arbitrary code evaluation.
An attacker must possess a valid project identifier from the target workspace to successfully target the vulnerable endpoint.
The command handler incorrectly assumes stateless operations do not require cross-site request forgery protection, omitting token verification before executing user-supplied expressions.
The patch introduces explicit cross-site request forgery token validation at the start of the request handler, rejecting unauthorized requests before expression evaluation.
Multiple HTTP endpoints in the plugin lack proper authorization checks, allowing low-privileged users to access sensitive configuration and credential data.
The vulnerability requires an attacker to possess global Job or Configure permissions, which are insufficient for accessing system-scoped credentials but were incorrectly granted access.
Several HTTP endpoints fail to verify that the requesting user holds the necessary administrative or configure permissions before exposing configuration IDs and credential mappings.
The patch introduces explicit permission verification calls to the affected endpoints to restrict access to authorized users and align with the principle of least privilege.
This function serves as the primary interface for registering constraint violations during the self-validation process.
The vulnerability manifests when developers pass user-controlled or untrusted data directly into the violation message parameter during self-validation.
The implementation directly forwards the provided message to the constraint violation template builder without sanitization, allowing embedded expression language syntax to be interpreted.
The patch modifies the message handling logic to apply an escaping function before template construction, ensuring special characters are neutralized.
The vulnerability is triggered when file ending parameters are assigned via configuration or setter methods prior to command execution.
The system dynamically constructs shell execution strings by substituting file path components directly into the command argument.
File ending values are concatenated into shell command strings without validation or escaping, enabling arbitrary command injection.
The patch introduces a sanitization step to validate and clean file ending values before assignment in both configuration and setter methods.
The method processes user-supplied resource identifiers to generate file URLs for application assets.
The application accepts external resource names that may contain path traversal sequences or remote file protocols without prior validation.
The implementation directly constructs URLs from untrusted input without verifying that the resolved path remains within the intended base directory.
The update normalizes the base directory path and verifies that the resolved file's absolute path starts with the expected directory before returning the URL.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

nodes.details: The method applies a naming strategy to rename properties during data binding introspection.
Deserialization processes properties using a naming strategy while some properties are annotated to be ignored.
The internal collection tracking ignored property names is not updated when a property name is transformed, causing the ignore check to fail for the new name.
The patch checks if a property being renamed was previously marked as ignored and explicitly adds the renamed name to the ignored properties collection.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Extension or Modification of Elements of an Object or Data Structure

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when user-supplied profile parameters are processed by the server configuration retrieval endpoints.
The vulnerability requires the configuration server to be set up with a native file system backend to enable directory traversal.
The profile parameter extracted from client requests lacks proper sanitization, allowing crafted paths to escape configured search directories.
The patch adds explicit validation checks for the profile parameter before repository access to reject invalid encoded locations.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The application exposes a public homepage that allows unauthenticated guests to download packaged data containing internal information.
The application's homepage is publicly accessible without requiring authentication, enabling guest users to initiate downloads.
Sensitive migration data documents are stored without visibility restrictions, allowing unauthorized actors to retrieve them through public access.
The patch modifies the data persistence logic to explicitly mark internal migration documents as hidden, preventing unauthorized public retrieval.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

nodes.details: The vulnerability affects cryptographic verification routines used during SCRAM authentication to validate client proofs and server signatures.
The implementation compares sensitive authentication material, such as client proofs and server signatures, against computed cryptographic values.

The code utilizes a standard array equality method that exits early upon the first mismatch, causing execution time to depend on matching bytes. This timing variation enables an attacker to infer sensitive authentication material through side-channel analysis.

The patch replaces the short-circuit comparison method with a constant-time equality check to ensure execution time remains independent of input data. This prevents timing-based side-channel attacks during secret verification.
The vulnerability is triggered when serializing deeply nested JSON structures through the node's string conversion method.
An attacker must supply a JSON payload with extreme nesting depth that is parsed into a node tree prior to output.
The original serialization logic relies on direct recursive traversal without depth limits, causing excessive resource consumption during output generation.
The patch introduces a dedicated stack-based iterator to replace direct recursion, thereby controlling traversal depth and preventing resource exhaustion.
Method is invoked during Java object deserialization to reconstruct internal state from an input stream.
An attacker supplies a crafted serialized object containing an untrusted length value during deserialization.
The implementation directly allocates a byte array using an attacker-controlled length without validation, causing excessive transient heap usage.
The patch replaces direct allocation with a helper method to validate the input length before memory allocation.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

nodes.details: The macro processes the server URL parameter to determine the target endpoint for diagram rendering.
The extension allows users to specify an alternative PlantUML server via a dedicated parameter, which is directly used for network requests.
The application fails to verify the supplied server URL against a configured list of trusted domains, allowing arbitrary network connections.
The patch introduces URL parsing and validates the target against a security manager, rejecting requests to untrusted domains with an exception.
The endpoint handles slice reconfiguration and serves as the target for the CSRF attack.
The endpoint accepts requests from any HTTP method, allowing attackers to trigger state-changing operations via cross-site requests.
The implementation processes form submissions without verifying the HTTP method, enabling unauthorized configuration changes through CSRF.
The patch adds an annotation to restrict the endpoint to POST requests only, preventing cross-site request forgery.
The vulnerability manifests during the initialization and management of the build output stream.
The issue occurs specifically when a build process executes without any defined operational steps.
Secret masking and cleanup were incorrectly bound to a lifecycle callback that fails to trigger when no steps are present.
The patch relocates the secret removal operation to the output stream closure method, ensuring execution during log finalization.
The HTTP endpoint retrieves available credentials identifiers without verifying user privileges, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive configuration data.
The original function executes credential lookup operations without validating whether the requesting user possesses the necessary administrative or item-level permissions.
The method directly returns a list of matching credentials identifiers to any caller, enabling attackers with basic read access to discover stored credential identifiers.
The update introduces explicit authorization validations for both global administration and specific item permissions before returning the credentials list to the client.
The vulnerability is triggered during the plugin's recursive file copying operation when archiving generated reports from agent workspaces to the controller.
An attacker must possess Item or Configure permissions on a Jenkins job to initiate the report publishing workflow.
The recursive copy operation fails to restrict symbolic links, causing invalid symlinks to be archived and recreated on the controller, which leaks path existence information.
The patch modifies the recursive copy logic to explicitly apply a no-follow-links option, preventing symbolic links from being archived or recreated.

nodes.details: The method iterates over constraint violations and applies custom checks to content objects during validation.
Validation logic is invoked when processing user objects to ensure data integrity and constraint compliance.
The initial implementation lacked a specific check to enforce maximum length constraints on user password attributes.
The patch adds a conditional verification to compare password length against a defined limit and appends an error message if the threshold is exceeded.
The method processes incoming NEW-ENVIRON subnegotiation data to populate the connection's environment map.
The vulnerability requires an unauthenticated client to initiate NEW-ENVIRON negotiation before login, allowing arbitrary variable injection.
The processing loop lacks a counter to restrict the number of variable pairs stored in the connection's environment map, enabling heap exhaustion.
The patch introduces a counter that increments per variable and aborts processing if the count exceeds a predefined maximum limit.
The vulnerability is triggered when the plugin serves archived report files through Jenkins' directory browser support mechanism.
The plugin configures a system property that instructs Jenkins to bypass its default Content-Security-Policy header for served resources.
Disabling the Content-Security-Policy header removes browser-side protections, allowing attackers to inject and execute malicious scripts via controlled static files.
The patch removes the system property assignment that disabled security headers, ensuring Jenkins applies its standard Content-Security-Policy to served files.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: This method serves as the web endpoint for populating credential selection dropdowns, acting as the primary attack surface for enumeration.
The vulnerability can be triggered by users possessing only Overall or Read permissions, which are insufficient for accessing sensitive credential metadata.
The endpoint failed to validate administrative privileges before querying the credential store, enabling unauthorized enumeration of stored credential identifiers.
The patch introduces a mandatory administrative permission check at the entrypoint and restricts credential retrieval to globally scoped items using proper authentication contexts.
The method parses and returns referenced parameter values used for dynamic UI generation within the plugin.
An attacker must possess Job/Configure permission to inject untrusted reference parameter values into the plugin settings.
The plugin fails to neutralize or escape reference parameter values before storing them, allowing raw script content to persist.
The patch introduces an escaping function to sanitize each parsed parameter value before it is added to the collection.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the property binder processes user-supplied input by parsing and evaluating it as a dynamic expression.
The binding mechanism initializes a fully capable evaluation context that permits arbitrary type resolution and method invocation during expression processing.
User-controlled property names are directly passed to the expression parser without validation, allowing attackers to inject malicious payloads that execute arbitrary code.
The patch replaces the unrestricted evaluation context with a restricted variant that limits property access and disables dangerous type resolution and method calls.
The vulnerability is triggered through the SAML authentication login service that processes incoming HTTP requests and handles SAML assertions.
The server must be configured with SAML authentication enabled, allowing the login service to parse and process SAML requests from clients.
The application extracts the redirect target URL from the incoming SAML request and uses it to generate a redirect form without validating the destination.
The patch modifies the authentication validation logic to accept an additional set of valid credentials and adjusts the encryption configuration settings.
These HTTP endpoints expose build artifact metadata without verifying sufficient user permissions.
The vulnerability is exploitable when the optional Run/Artifacts permission configuration is activated on the system.
The implementation fails to validate whether the requesting user holds the required Run/Artifacts permissions before exposing artifact information.
The patch introduces explicit permission validation calls before processing artifact requests to restrict access to authorized users only.
The vulnerability is triggered when instantiating a JSONObject from a raw JSON string, specifically during the tokenization and key-value parsing phases.
The vulnerability requires a crafted JSON string containing control characters or nested structures that exploit the tokenizer state machine to bypass standard validation checks.
The parser fails to verify stream termination after processing separators, allowing crafted inputs to bypass boundary checks and trigger exponential memory allocation during key serialization.
The patch introduces an explicit validation step after processing separators to verify if the input stream has ended, throwing a syntax error if the expected closing delimiter is missing.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

nodes.details: The method initializes and returns a DocumentBuilder used to parse XML property lists, serving as the primary interface for document processing.
The vulnerability requires a local attacker to trigger XML parsing through the document builder, which processes external entities during DTD resolution.
The XML parser's entity resolver fails to block all external resource references, allowing an attacker to trigger XML external entity processing during document construction.
The patch replaces the inline entity resolver with a dedicated resolver class to strictly control DTD resolution and prevent unauthorized external entity access.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The method serves as a configuration test interface for external service connectivity.
The validation routine executes without verifying user privileges, permitting low-privileged accounts to trigger it.
The endpoint allows arbitrary network requests and cross-site requests without authentication or method restrictions.
The update introduces a mandatory POST constraint and validates administrative permissions before processing the request.
The vulnerability is triggered during the SAML authentication flow when the finish login endpoint processes the authenticated request.
An attacker must be able to control the session identifier before the user completes the authentication process.
The application fails to invalidate or recreate the HTTP session after successful authentication, allowing a fixed session ID to persist.
The patch introduces session recreation upon login completion and validates the redirect target to prevent session fixation and open redirect risks.
The vulnerability is triggered during the initialization of HTTP/2 stream channels when the client processes redirect responses.
The HTTP client must be explicitly configured to automatically follow redirects, which activates the specific code path for chained redirect scenarios.
The stream handler configuration incorrectly handles credential state during channel initialization, allowing sensitive authentication data to leak across redirect boundaries.
The patch alters the stream handler setup calls by introducing a new boolean argument to explicitly control credential forwarding behavior during channel initialization.
This method initializes JavaMail properties for SMTP connections, including TLS and authentication settings.
The vulnerability manifests when connecting to an SMTP server over TLS in plugin versions prior to 2.76, where hostname verification is not enforced by default.
The configuration logic omits setting the SSL server identity verification property, allowing connections to proceed without verifying the server certificate against the intended hostname.
The patch introduces a default configuration to enforce server identity verification when TLS is active, mitigating man-in-the-middle attack risks.
The method retrieves the display name of a project to be rendered in the web interface.
An attacker must possess the ability to configure Jenkins jobs to inject malicious content into the project display name.
The method directly returns the project display name without sanitizing HTML entities, enabling stored cross-site scripting in the web interface.
The patch applies HTML escaping to the project display name before returning it, neutralizing any injected scripts.

nodes.details: The vulnerability originates from how the plugin handles and persists API credentials during job configuration.
Jobs configured with older plugin versions retain unencrypted credential fields in their configuration data.
Sensitive authentication values were stored and retrieved as plain text strings, allowing direct disk access to expose them.
