nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the Git plugin binds username and password credentials to environment variables during a build execution.
The issue manifests when the Git plugin's username and password binding feature is utilized to inject credentials into the build environment.
The credential binding method had its secret and public value maps passed in the wrong order, causing the masking mechanism to fail and expose credentials in logs.
The fix corrects the parameter order in the binding method and adds verification steps to ensure credentials are properly replaced with asterisks in build logs.
The exposed web method modifies agent configuration by attaching a public IP address.
The endpoint allows execution by users with only read-level privileges and accepts GET requests.
The operation performs a data modification without validating user authorization or request method constraints.
The patch enforces POST-only requests and requires the Computer.CONFIGURE permission before execution.
The function processes hypervisor connection parameters and is exposed to external requests, serving as the initial point of exploitation.
Attackers must hold Overall/Read permission to reach the endpoint and initiate the connection verification process.
The endpoint lacks a sufficient privilege verification step, allowing lower-privileged users to initiate connections and capture stored credentials.
The intended fix introduces a permission validation step to restrict endpoint access, as indicated by the vulnerability description.
Processes GraphQL responses over WebSocket connections, managing subscription state and error encoding.
The vulnerability applies to applications that have explicitly enabled the WebSocket transport mechanism for GraphQL communication.
The handler lacks sufficient validation to prevent unauthorized cross-origin WebSocket connections, allowing session hijacking.
The patch introduces a cleanup hook to explicitly release underlying data buffers when WebSocket messages are discarded.
The add method in the thread-safe cookie store serves as the primary entry point for processing and persisting incoming cookies.
Applications utilizing a single shared cookie store instance to communicate with both trusted and untrusted hosts create the necessary conditions for cross-domain cookie injection.
The storage logic fails to verify whether the responding host is permitted to set a cookie for the domain specified in the attribute, allowing unauthorized cookie planting.
The update introduces a validation step that discards cookies when the specified domain does not match the requesting host, aligning with standard cookie handling protocols.
The JDBC driver performs server certificate validation during connection establishment to verify the server's identity.
The driver relies on a custom string parsing routine to extract the Common Name from the certificate subject distinguished name for hostname matching.
The manual parsing logic fails to securely isolate the Common Name attribute, allowing malformed or ambiguous certificate data to bypass validation and enable network spoofing.
The patch replaces the manual string parsing with standard LDAP and RDN APIs to accurately extract the Common Name and applies consistent case normalization for reliable hostname verification.
The vulnerability is triggered during the discovery and processing of pull requests from forks in Bitbucket Server.
The issue occurs when the plugin discovers pull requests originating from forks within the same account on Bitbucket Server.
The code incorrectly constructs the SCM head object using the target repository's owner and name instead of the source repository's metadata, bypassing trust policy checks.
The patch updates the hook processors to extract and use the source repository's owner and name when instantiating the SCM head object for forked pull requests.
Multiple Subversion plugin methods handle form validation and submission without HTTP method restrictions.
Validation and submission methods accept GET requests by default, allowing unauthenticated or unauthorized cross-origin requests.
The absence of POST enforcement annotations on validation methods permits attackers to forge requests to arbitrary URLs.
Adding POST requirement annotations restricts these endpoints to POST requests only, mitigating CSRF risks.
The vulnerability occurs within the archive header reading routine when processing nested subheaders.
An attacker must supply a crafted RAR archive containing invalid or corrupt header structures to trigger the flaw.
The parsing logic proceeds to a switch statement without verifying the subheader type, allowing malformed data to cause an infinite loop.
The patch adds a null check for the subheader type prior to the switch statement to safely abort processing of invalid headers.
The vulnerability impacts endpoints managing Docker connections and credentials that lack proper access validation.
Exploitation requires only Overall/Read access to the Jenkins instance to trigger the vulnerable methods.
Sensitive endpoints failed to verify user permissions before executing Docker commands or exposing credential lists.
The update adds explicit ADMINISTER permission checks and enforces POST methods to prevent unauthorized requests.
The method processes configuration properties directly from incoming HTTP request parameters without initial validation.
The application must have an OpenID Connect authenticator configured to process incoming authentication requests and configuration overrides.
The configuration retrieval method accepts arbitrary keys from request parameters and overrides internal settings without validation, allowing untrusted input to modify authentication behavior.
The patch introduces a containment check to ensure only predefined safe properties can be overridden via request parameters, preventing unauthorized configuration changes.
The validation endpoint processes a user-supplied query parameter and returns an HTTP response containing the parameter value within an error message.
The application directly incorporates the unescaped query parameter into an HTML error response without proper input sanitization.
The code utilizes a markup-enabled response method to embed the exception message directly into HTML, allowing malicious script injection.
The patch replaces the markup-enabled response method with a plain text alternative to prevent HTML interpretation of the error message.

nodes.details: This method serves as the web interface for testing server connectivity using provided credentials.

The absence of request method enforcement and permission checks allowed attackers to forge requests that execute credential validation.
The patch introduces method restriction and permission verification to prevent unauthorized cross-site requests from triggering the connection test.
The tar extraction function processes archive entries without validating their target paths.
A user imports a crafted tar archive containing entries with relative paths that escape the extraction root.
The extraction logic directly uses archive entry names to construct file paths without verifying they remain within the intended destination directory.
The patch adds a normalization check to ensure the resolved destination path starts with the target directory path, throwing an exception if it escapes.

The fix restores the path sanitization function to validate and restrict file output paths before writing.

The download logic fails to extract expected checksums from metadata or verify the downloaded file's integrity.
The patch extracts expected checksums from plugin metadata and validates the downloaded file before proceeding.

nodes.details: The application initializes an internal system user with static credentials directly embedded in the source code during startup and event handling.
System user authentication parameters are statically defined in the codebase and passed directly to service methods without external configuration.
Static username and password values are embedded directly in the application logic, allowing trivial authentication and unauthorized data access.
The update replaces static credentials with dynamic parameters and enforces runtime validation through environment variables to eliminate hard-coded secrets.
The vulnerability is triggered when the plugin processes uploaded coverage reports to generate output files.
An attacker must be able to control the contents of the coverage report file to inject malicious paths.
The plugin directly uses unvalidated file paths from the report to construct output locations without restricting directory traversal.
The patch applies filename sanitization to restrict output paths to the intended base directory and prevents directory escape.

The extraction routine directly uses archive entry names to construct destination file paths without prior validation of their structure or safety.
The implementation fails to verify that the resolved absolute path of the destination file remains strictly within the intended extraction directory, enabling path traversal.
The patch adds a check to detect relative traversal sequences and validates that the canonical destination path starts with the canonical work directory path before proceeding.

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during automatic HTTP request processing where the client's managed cookie store intercepts and modifies outgoing requests.

The implementation unconditionally overwrites existing request cookies with matching names from the store, disregarding explicitly client-provided values.
The patch replaces the unconditional overwrite method with a conditional addition method that preserves explicitly set cookies and only adds store cookies if unset.
The vulnerability is triggered when an administrator submits configuration values for system paths through the web administration interface.
The attacker must first compromise or obtain credentials for an administrative account to access the configuration management interface.
The system previously treated path configuration values as generic strings without validating their format or rejecting malicious characters, allowing injection attacks.
The patch changes the configuration type to PATH and introduces a validator that uses standard path parsing to reject invalid inputs and prevent injection.
This method is responsible for creating and caching the cryptographic provider used to encrypt stored secrets.
An attacker with read-only access to the secret storage backend can observe existing encrypted data and attempt to craft valid replacements.
The provider was instantiated using a standard constructor that lacked strict binding to the expected cryptographic key, allowing potential key substitution or ciphertext manipulation.
The patch replaces direct instantiation with a builder pattern that explicitly calls a strict construction method using the expected key identifier, ensuring only the authorized key is accepted.
The code path processes constructor parameters annotated with external type information during JSON deserialization.
Deserialization involves a constructor parameter annotated with both view restrictions and external type information.
The external type ID processing logic fails to verify if a creator property is visible in the active JSON view before binding its value.
The patch introduces active view checks to skip or continue processing properties that are not visible in the current view context.
The parse method processes incoming XML dependency reports using an XML digester to extract vulnerability data.
Attackers must be able to control workspace contents to supply a crafted XML file for the parser to process.
The XML parser lacked configuration to restrict external entity resolution and DTD loading, allowing XXE exploitation.
The patch configures the digester to disallow DOCTYPE declarations and disable external general and parameter entities along with external DTD loading.

Response headers are populated with arbitrary user-supplied data without validation or sanitization.

The application fails to properly sanitize or validate uploaded SVG files, allowing embedded malicious scripts to be stored server-side.
The patch introduces a conditional check on the image type before processing, restricting execution to valid image formats.

Form validation methods did not enforce administrative privileges or CSRF protection, enabling attackers to submit arbitrary credentials to the configured endpoint.

The function accepts user-supplied URLs and credentials to verify connectivity to an external service.
Attackers possessing only Overall/Read permissions can reach the endpoint without proper authorization.
The function fails to verify administrative privileges before executing connection tests with arbitrary inputs.
The update introduces a permission verification step to ensure only administrators can invoke the connection test functionality.

An attacker must successfully connect to the agent's named pipe to initiate the remote command execution workflow.

Processes HTTP requests to validate build log patterns against console output.
Malicious actors can inject scripts into build console logs that are subsequently used for pattern testing.
The validation endpoint returns user-supplied matching text directly using a method that interprets HTML markup, bypassing necessary sanitization.
The patch replaces the markup-rendering response method with a standard text method to prevent browser execution of injected content.

The implementation lacks restrictions on file paths and fails to disable external entity resolution, enabling XML external entity injection attacks.
The patch modifies the callable execution type and removes the placeholder security check to enforce proper execution boundaries and restrict file path access.

The patch adds a check to detect when the closing bracket is not found and explicitly terminates parsing to prevent invalid index handling.
The utility method processes template strings and context data to generate output, acting as the primary interface for rendering user-supplied content.
The original implementation explicitly configured the underlying template engine to bypass HTML escaping during compilation.
Without HTML escaping, arbitrary script tags embedded in context values are directly injected into the generated output, enabling cross-site scripting attacks.
The patch refactors the method to accept a boolean parameter that controls whether HTML escaping is applied, introducing a safe rendering path.

nodes.details: This routine determines method inheritance relationships to support annotation scanning.
Security mechanisms depend on correctly identifying overridden methods across inheritance chains to locate applicable annotations.
The override comparison fails to accurately match parameter types across hierarchies, causing security annotations to be overlooked during runtime evaluation.
The update replaces the generic resolution mechanism with a direct class extraction to guarantee accurate parameter type alignment during inheritance checks.
The vulnerability is triggered when the XMPReader.read method parses XMP metadata from an uploaded image file.
An attacker must supply an image file containing a malicious XMP segment that gets parsed by the application.
The DocumentBuilderFactory is instantiated using newInstance() without disabling external entity processing, allowing XXE attacks.
The patch replaces DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() with a custom createDocumentBuilderFactory() method to apply secure parsing defaults.
This method configures LDAP security environment variables for user authentication.

The authentication strategy only updates environment variables without triggering a reconnection, causing the LDAP server to ignore the provided credentials and allow authentication with arbitrary passwords.
The patch adds an explicit reconnection call to ensure the LDAP server processes the newly set credentials and enforces the authentication bind.

A custom Safelist must permit raw-text elements, and the input HTML must contain a tag name ending in a control character.
The parser incorrectly normalizes or trims control characters from tag names, causing them to match different elements and altering serialization behavior.
The fix replaces the tag name normalization logic with a simple case conversion to ensure control characters in tag names are preserved during parsing.
The vulnerability is triggered during the parsing of application configuration files where dynamic component instantiation is automatically registered.
An attacker must compromise a configuration file or inject a malicious environment variable pointing to a compromised configuration file.
The framework automatically registers a dynamic evaluation component as a default nested element, allowing untrusted configuration files to trigger arbitrary code execution.
The patch removes the automatic registration of the dynamic evaluation component as a default nested element to prevent untrusted configurations from instantiating it.
The authorized endpoint processes a GET parameter that is directly embedded into the response output without validation.
The vulnerability requires the specific extension to be installed and the corresponding endpoint to be accessible.
User-controlled input is rendered verbatim within a script context inside a template, allowing arbitrary code execution.
The update applies HTML escaping to user-supplied data before embedding it in template contexts to neutralize injected scripts.

The credential dropdown population methods lacked authorization validation, allowing unauthorized users to view or select credentials.
The patch adds explicit permission checks for credential creation and update before populating the dropdown lists.
The vulnerability is triggered when the framework processes incoming GraphQL requests containing variable maps.
The attack requires the application to expose paginated connection fields and have exploitable classes available on the classpath for deserialization.
The framework incorrectly handles untrusted variable maps during request processing, allowing malicious payloads to trigger unsafe deserialization and remote code execution.
The patch updates variable map type signatures to explicitly declare nullable object values, ensuring stricter type handling during request processing.
The plugin establishes connections to Service Virtualization servers where certificate validation is bypassed.
Plugin versions 6.7 and earlier automatically disabled SSL/TLS certificate validation for all server connections without user configuration.
The server connection logic lacked a configurable parameter to control certificate validation, causing it to be permanently disabled.
The patch introduces a trust configuration parameter to server settings and executor factories, enabling explicit control over SSL/TLS certificate validation.
The responder constructs file paths using request parameters without validation, allowing access outside the intended directory.
The component processes file names and resource identifiers directly from HTTP requests without verifying their containment within the allowed directory.
The original implementation concatenates user-supplied strings into a file path without resolving symlinks or checking for traversal sequences.
The patch resolves the constructed path to its canonical absolute form and verifies it remains within the base directory before use.

nodes.details: The application constructs database connection strings by directly incorporating user-supplied configuration values into the URL template.
The data source interface permits users to specify arbitrary connection parameters that are appended to the database connection string.
The configuration logic fails to sanitize or validate user-provided parameters before embedding them into the connection string, enabling injection of malicious options.
The update adds a validation loop that checks the provided parameters against a predefined list of dangerous options and aborts the connection if a match is found.
The method constructs a file path using an external identifier to locate a sensitive credential file within a designated directory.
An attacker must be able to control the input parameter passed to the file lookup function, typically through a compromised agent process.
The implementation directly uses the unvalidated input as a filename component without checking for directory traversal sequences.
The patch introduces a validation check to reject inputs containing forward or backslash characters, ensuring the file remains within the intended directory.

The patch configures the document builder factory to restrict external DTD and schema access by setting their corresponding attributes to empty strings.

Transaction invocation objects are added to an internal tracker but fail to be removed when exceptions occur, causing uncontrolled accumulation.
The patch adds a finally block to explicitly remove the invocation object from the tracker, preventing memory and resource leaks.
The vulnerability is triggered during the processing of input stream chunks to determine if more data is available.
The input stream supplies a chunk length value without prior validation before buffer allocation.
The allocation logic directly uses the unvalidated length to create a buffer, permitting invalid values to trigger fatal exceptions.
The update introduces a negative value check and wraps buffer allocation in error handling to prevent uncaught fatal exceptions.

The patch applies JavaScript escaping to all artifact metadata inputs to neutralize potential script injection before storage.

The patch modifies the execution flow to pass the interpreter context and raw script directly to the security enforcement module, ensuring restrictions are applied during compilation and execution.

The assembler subtracts the received payload length from the expected remaining bytes without first validating that the payload fits within the declared size, causing the counter to underflow and throw an unhandled exception.

The implementation utilizes a permissive legacy API for temporary file generation, which exposes file contents to potential unauthorized access.
The diff replaces the legacy file creation method with a modern API to enforce stricter security constraints during temporary file generation.

This constructor serves as the initialization point for the canonicalization method and is where the validation logic was introduced to prevent arbitrary algorithm specification.
The constructor previously accepted any TransformService or XML element without verifying if the specified canonicalization algorithm was permitted or secure.
The absence of checks for the canonicalization algorithm type or identifier permits attackers to inject arbitrary weak algorithms, compromising signature integrity.
The patch introduces a conditional check that throws an exception if the service is not an instance of the expected canonicalizer or does not match a valid algorithm identifier.
The cryptographic routine processes incoming messages and signature parameters to authenticate data integrity.
The verification process accepts external signature components without enforcing mathematical constraints prior to computation.
The implementation omits checks to ensure signature values remain within the valid cryptographic range, enabling forgery attacks.
The patch introduces explicit boundary validations to reject signature components that fall outside the acceptable mathematical interval.
The form filler method exposes stored credential identifiers to users without verifying their access rights.
The function lacks permission validation before querying and returning credential data, allowing basic read access to bypass restrictions.
System-level credential lookup is performed without caller authentication, enabling unauthorized enumeration of sensitive identifiers.
The patch introduces explicit access control checks for administrative and item-level permissions, returning an empty model when authorization fails.
This endpoint processes HTTP requests to trigger project release builds using provided configuration parameters.
The submission handler accepted incoming requests without verifying their origin or requiring explicit user confirmation.
The method processed sensitive build configuration parameters without checking user permissions or request authenticity.
The patch introduces explicit permission verification calls across multiple methods and restricts the submission handler to POST requests only.
The vulnerability resides in the HTTP/HTTPS endpoint argument resolvers that process incoming Amazon SNS notification payloads.
Incoming SNS messages are accepted and processed by the application without any cryptographic validation of their origin.
The message handling logic bypasses signature checks, allowing attackers to forge HTTP POST requests that mimic legitimate SNS notifications.
The patch integrates an optional message manager component to invoke signature verification on the raw content before argument resolution proceeds.
The SAML plugin implements an extension point to selectively disable CSRF protection for specific URLs.

The patch replaces the substring search with a strict prefix check and verifies the active security realm before applying the exclusion.

An attacker truncates the outer message body at a non-final segment boundary, causing the receiver to process an incomplete sequence.
The parsing logic fails to validate that a designated final segment was explicitly received before concluding the stream processing loop.
The patch introduces a flag to track whether a final segment marker was encountered and raises an error if the stream ends without it.
The vulnerability impacts the POST /api/import and POST /api/export endpoints within the application.
The security filter chain applies authorization rules only when the external identity provider integration is active.
The authorization chain uses incorrect path patterns and misplaces role requirements, allowing non-administrators to bypass access controls.
The patch corrects the request matcher patterns and explicitly assigns the administrator role requirement to the affected endpoints.
This method processes incoming HTTP requests to extract session identifiers from headers.

The implementation directly outputs the extracted session identifier to the standard output stream during request resolution.
The patch eliminates the direct standard output logging call to prevent session identifiers from being written to application logs.

The parser operates in a non-blocking mode receiving data in small chunks without a terminating character, preventing immediate value completion.

The application processes user-supplied template expressions without validating or restricting dangerous built-in operators.

The patch configures a safer built-in class resolver to block dangerous class instantiation while maintaining backward compatibility.
The vulnerability is triggered when the server processes and delivers watch events to connected clients via network connection handlers.

The server fails to validate access control lists before delivering watch events, allowing unauthorized clients to receive znode path notifications.
The patch introduces an explicit ACL verification step within the event processing method, returning early if the client lacks read permissions for the target znode.

The patch restricts the endpoint to POST requests and adds an administrative permission check to prevent unauthorized access and CSRF attacks.

nodes.summary: replace magic constant with typed password
nodes.details: The patch replaces the string-based magic constant with a dedicated password interface and implementation, ensuring proper credential validation and preventing cache key collisions.

The patch replaces the direct blacklist check with a call to SubTypeValidator.instance().validateSubType to enforce stricter type validation.

The deserialization methods fail to validate array nesting depth, allowing recursive parsing of deeply nested structures without bounds.
The patch introduces explicit token checks to detect nested START_ARRAY tokens and immediately terminates processing to prevent infinite recursion.
The eval method processes and executes user-provided Groovy scripts, handling their return values before output.

The original implementation only sanitized return values if they were CharSequence instances, leaving List and Map objects unescaped and vulnerable to stored XSS.
The patch replaces the type-specific check with a generic resolution method to ensure all legal return values from sandboxed scripts are properly escaped.
The vulnerability is triggered during the startup and shutdown phases of the Oort and Seti components, where channel listeners and authorization rules are registered and removed.
The system utilizes Oort and Seti channels to facilitate internal cluster traffic and synchronize state across distributed nodes.
Internal Oort and Seti channels are created without restrictive access controls, permitting unauthenticated remote users to subscribe and publish arbitrary messages.
The fix applies a global channel filter and dedicated protection routines during service initialization and termination to explicitly restrict unauthorized access to internal channels.
This method serves as the primary authorization check point for validating user access to Jenkins items.

The validation logic only verifies whether a type is an array, failing to recursively unwrap nested arrays and validate the innermost element type against the configured allowlist.
The patch modifies the validation method to recursively unwrap nested arrays, extract the component type, and apply allowlist checks or permit only primitives, interfaces, and abstract classes.
The method accepts user-controlled string content and directly passes it to the JAXB unmarshaller for XML parsing.

The application allows scripts to be provided via network requests and dynamically compiled for execution.
Malicious code can be embedded within user scripts that are directly compiled and executed without proper validation.
The patch escapes special delimiter characters in embedded script documentation and adjusts script inclusion flags to prevent injection.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during the OAuth2 authentication callback where the application determines the post-login redirect destination.
The authentication endpoint accepts user-controlled values for redirect targets through query parameters and HTTP headers.
The implementation assigns user-supplied redirect URLs to the response even when they fail safety verification, permitting arbitrary external redirection.
The update delegates redirect URL resolution to a dedicated method that enforces strict validation, ensuring only internal Jenkins URLs are used.
The vulnerability enables an attacker to gain unauthorized access to arbitrary recordings or rooms.
The flaw is triggered through standard application workflows involving invitation or OAuth2 management components.
A flawed comparison mechanism fails to properly validate access permissions, allowing unauthorized resource retrieval.
The patch consolidates database query execution into single return statements and simplifies test initialization to address the underlying access control flaw.
The vulnerability is triggered during the WebAuthn authentication flow when the provider processes the authentication token and authenticator data.
An authenticator returns an incremented signature counter value during the authentication phase.
The implementation instantiates a new wrapper object instead of utilizing the original authenticator instance, preventing the updated counter value from being properly persisted.
The patch replaces the newly instantiated wrapper with the original authenticator reference to ensure state updates are correctly tracked and persisted.
The vulnerability originates during user session initialization where authentication rights are assigned to the active session.
An attacker must first gain access to certain private information to exploit the authentication bypass.
The session initialization logic incorrectly treats empty rights sets identically to null values, allowing unauthorized privilege assignment or user impersonation.
The patch modifies the conditional check to only evaluate null rights, preventing empty sets from triggering the fallback rights retrieval mechanism.
The descriptor methods handling key path validation and connection testing expose endpoints for verifying SSH host and credential configurations.
Attackers possessing only Overall/Read access can invoke the connection testing endpoints without triggering authorization failures.
The methods lack a mandatory permission verification before processing user-supplied SSH connection parameters, allowing unauthorized execution.
The patch introduces a mandatory administrative permission check and restricts requests to POST methods to prevent unauthorized access.
The service method responsible for initializing and persisting authentication data for an internal operational account.
The initialization routine originally bound the account password directly to a static identifier during setup.
Embedding static authentication data in the source code enables trivial unauthorized access to sensitive internal APIs and configuration endpoints.
The update eliminates static password binding, enforces runtime configuration through environment variables, and ensures credential rotation upon initialization.
The vulnerability occurs within the dedicated JavaScript escaping routines that process user-supplied strings before embedding them in script contexts.
HTML templates utilizing script tags or attributes with JavaScript template literals are processed without adequate character sanitization.
The escape routines fail to handle backtick and dollar sign characters, allowing attackers to inject malicious code that breaks string boundaries or triggers interpolation.
The patch introduces explicit case handlers to escape backticks and dollar signs using appropriate escape sequences, preventing template literal injection.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Escape Characters in a Web Page

nodes.details: This method processes XML strings provided by build step inputs, serving as the direct execution point for document generation.
Attackers can supply crafted XML documents through Jenkins build step inputs, which are directly passed to the parsing routine.
The XML parser is instantiated without disabling external entity resolution or DTD processing, allowing XXE exploitation.
The update configures the document builder factory to explicitly disable DOCTYPE declarations, external entities, DTD loading, and XInclude features.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The function handles cryptographic key generation during decryption processing by resolving algorithms from data reference URIs.
The vulnerability manifests when cryptographic algorithm resolution or key initialization fails during the decryption of encrypted keys or message data.
The original code immediately propagates cryptographic exceptions, inadvertently leaking decryption failure details that attackers exploit to recover symmetric keys.
The patch intercepts all initialization failures and falls back to a standard AES-128 key generation, preventing algorithm-specific attacks and suppressing error leakage.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the application receives serialized data over a Java Socket and processes it through an ObjectInputStream.
The system accepts external data transmitted over a network connection without performing any preliminary security checks or class validation.
Incoming socket data is directly deserialized into Java objects without verifying the allowed class types, enabling arbitrary code execution.
The patch implements a serialization whitelist to explicitly permit only safe classes during the deserialization process, blocking malicious payloads.
The method retrieves the release version string used to populate the badge tooltip in the Jenkins UI.
The vulnerability requires an attacker with Release permission to set a release version containing malicious script content.
The method returns the raw version string without applying XML escaping, enabling stored cross-site scripting when rendered in the UI.
The fix conditionally applies XML escaping to the version string before returning it to prevent script injection.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during the deserialization of the LoggingEventVO class via its readObject method, which processes incoming serialized payloads.
Exploitation requires the logback receiver component to be actively deployed, as it is responsible for handling and deserializing external data streams.
The deserialization routine fails to verify the size of the argument array before memory allocation, allowing attackers to specify excessively large or negative values that cause resource exhaustion.
The patch introduces a bounds validation check to reject array lengths that exceed a predefined safe threshold, throwing an exception to prevent denial-of-service conditions.
The vulnerability is triggered when the system processes command-line arguments received over SSH connections for repository operations.
Exploitation requires the attacker to possess basic read permissions on the controller, as the parser automatically processes arguments containing specific character sequences.
The command parser is configured to automatically substitute the at-sign character followed by a path with the corresponding file's contents, bypassing access controls.
The update explicitly configures the argument parser to disable the at-sign syntax feature, preventing automatic substitution of file paths with their contents.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The vulnerability originates in the plugin's connection and configuration methods that manage SSL/TLS certificate validation settings.
The plugin previously disabled SSL/TLS certificate validation by default, leaving connections susceptible to interception.
SSL/TLS certificate validation was not enforced by default in the connection logic, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.

The patch updates connection configuration to explicitly handle certificate validation settings and enables validation by default, while adding POST requirements and permission checks to secure endpoints.
The method processes global configuration settings for external service connections via HTTP requests.
The handler accepts configuration requests without restricting HTTP methods or validating request origins.
Authentication logic executes using user-supplied credentials without verifying administrative privileges or request integrity.
The update introduces a POST requirement and validates administrative permissions before executing the validation logic.
The vulnerability is triggered when the Jenkins Matrix Project plugin renders the label configuration interface for matrix builds.
Users with Agent or Configure permissions can define custom label names and descriptions that are subsequently rendered in the web interface.
The rendering function directly embeds user-supplied label names and descriptions into HTML and JavaScript strings without neutralizing special characters, enabling stored cross-site scripting.
The patch applies dedicated HTML attribute and JavaScript string escaping routines to all user-provided label attributes before they are concatenated into the generated markup.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when a build step attempts to retrieve and copy artifacts from a source project during job execution.
The vulnerability exists in plugin versions prior to 1.44, where default configuration retains insufficient access control mechanisms for cross-project artifact retrieval.
The original implementation fails to properly verify read permissions on the target source job, allowing unauthorized users to bypass visibility restrictions.
The patch introduces rigorous permission verification during artifact retrieval, adds a migration mode for backward compatibility, and enforces strict access checks in production mode.
This method processes incoming HTTP requests to persist user configuration data.
The vulnerability can be exploited by attackers who only possess Overall/Read permission.
The handler fails to verify sufficient user permissions before allowing modifications to global configuration settings.
The patch introduces a RequirePOST annotation to restrict the handler to POST requests, preventing unauthorized state changes.
The vulnerability resides in the core decompression routines for LZ4 and Snappy formats, which process compressed streams and write to an output buffer.
The issue manifests when applications allocate a fixed-size output buffer and reuse it across multiple decompression calls without clearing its contents beforehand.
The decompressors fail to validate that the computed match address strictly precedes the current output position, allowing crafted inputs to reference the current buffer location.
The patch adds boundary checks to ensure the match address is strictly less than the current output pointer, preventing reads from the current buffer position.
Processes form submissions to configure and trigger project builds with specified parameters.
The endpoint accepts incoming HTTP requests without verifying the request method, allowing external origins to interact with it.
The handler processes form data and schedules builds without requiring the POST method, enabling cross-site request forgery attacks.
Applies a method restriction annotation to the submission handler to ensure only POST requests are processed.
The vulnerability is triggered when users access HTTP endpoints to download or delete previously created support bundles.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to possess the deprecated bundle download permission, which was previously granted to users without administrative privileges.
The code incorrectly verifies the legacy bundle permission instead of the administrative permission, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive diagnostic data.
The patch replaces the legacy bundle permission check with a strict check for the administrative permission across all relevant endpoints.
These endpoints handle credential enumeration and configuration queries without prior access control.
Attackers only require Overall/Read access to Jenkins to trigger the vulnerable endpoints.
The affected HTTP endpoints lack proper permission verification, allowing low-privilege users to enumerate credentials.
The patch adds explicit permission checks and HTTP method restrictions to restrict endpoint access to authorized users.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during the parsing and instantiation of Java objects from untrusted JSON payloads.
The application relies on the jackson-databind library to deserialize external JSON data into Java objects without sufficient validation.
The deserialization process fails to properly validate all potential object types, allowing malicious gadget chains to bypass existing security blacklists.
The patch modifies type resolution and deserialization flow logic to enforce stricter validation and correct error handling, preventing bypass of security restrictions.
The vulnerability is triggered when the XHTML parser processes hyperlinks, specifically through the reference tag handler and comment handler that manage link labels and parameters.
The XHTML syntax parser previously relied on an external syntax that permitted raw HTML content, allowing arbitrary scripts to be embedded within link labels.
The parser directly passed raw link label content through the dependent syntax without proper filtering, enabling arbitrary script injection via specially crafted link labels.
The patch removes the dependency on the vulnerable external syntax by replacing the print renderer with a dedicated generator listener and routing link labels through a safe inline filter listener.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: Serves as a web endpoint that populates a selection list based on user-provided parameters.
The endpoint accepts GET requests, allowing users with read access to trigger it without additional authentication checks.
Lack of request method restriction enables cross-site request forgery, allowing attackers to force credential capture via forged requests.
Adds a request method restriction annotation to the endpoint to prevent unauthorized GET requests and mitigate CSRF attacks.
The POST endpoint for modifying application information processes update requests containing an identifier and new credentials.
The vulnerability is triggered when a request includes a valid identifier for an existing record, directing execution to the update branch.
The update logic directly overwrites stored credentials with request data without verifying the current password, enabling unauthorized modifications.
The patch adds a validation step that compares the submitted previous password against the stored value, rejecting mismatches to prevent unauthorized changes.
Processes and reparses canonicalized signed information elements during XML signature validation.
Triggered when an XML document employs a non-standard canonicalization algorithm that requires subtree reparsing.
The XML parser instance allocated for reparsing was not consistently returned to the resource pool, enabling potential resource exhaustion and signature validation bypass.
Encapsulates the parsing and document modification logic within a finally block to ensure the parser is always safely returned to the pool, preserving resource integrity and validation security.
The vulnerability is triggered during the server connection test process when establishing an HTTPS connection.

nodes.summary: https connection with insecure ssl bypass
nodes.details: The vulnerability occurs when the plugin attempts to establish an HTTPS connection and applies a global SSL certificate bypass mechanism.
The code previously applied an all-trusting trust manager and hostname verifier globally to the HTTPS connection class, disabling certificate validation for all connections.

nodes.summary: scope ssl bypass to specific connection
nodes.details: The fix replaces global SSL configuration methods with per-connection setters and introduces a conditional flag to control whether SSL validation is bypassed.
The method processes incoming HTTP requests to notify the Jenkins Subversion plugin about repository changes, serving as the primary attack surface for unauthorized access.
An attacker with network connectivity can directly interact with the endpoint without needing valid credentials, leveraging the lack of access controls to extract sensitive repository data.

The endpoint was intentionally left unguarded to simplify script configuration, resulting in a lack of proper access control that allowed unauthorized users to trigger notifications and expose information.
The patch replaces the manual request check with a standardized annotation to enforce proper request validation and prevent unauthorized invocation of the endpoint.
The macro processes XML responses from user-specified JIRA server URLs to render issue data.
An authenticated user must be able to edit their user profile wiki page to inject the malicious macro configuration.
The XML parser processes external DOCTYPE declarations and entity references from untrusted server responses without validation.
The patch restricts XML parsing to prevent resolution of external entities and DOCTYPE declarations from untrusted sources.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered through the user management endpoint that processes and returns user data.
The application previously enforced a length restriction but lacked character-level validation. This oversight allowed malicious payloads to bypass restrictions.
The application fails to validate or sanitize special characters in user-provided fields, enabling script injection.
The patch introduces explicit checks to reject inputs containing dangerous characters like angle brackets.
The method initializes an XML schema factory to validate embedded LWM2M schemas during DDF file processing.
The vulnerability is triggered when the application parses untrusted DDF files containing malicious XML content without prior validation.
The schema factory is instantiated without enabling secure processing features or restricting external DTD access, allowing XXE attacks.
The patch replaces direct instantiation with a dedicated method to ensure secure processing features and external resource restrictions are properly applied.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The vulnerability manifests during plugin build operations where sensitive configuration values are processed and persisted.
The plugin persists API keys, passwords, and UKeys directly into job configuration files without applying encryption mechanisms.
Sensitive credentials are stored and retrieved as plain strings, resulting in unencrypted data being written to the master file system.
The patch modifies credential getters to return encrypted secret types and explicitly extracts plaintext only when required for external API calls.
The vulnerability is triggered when the connector initializes XML transformation and parsing factories to process web service requests and responses.
The application initializes XML processing factories without disabling external resource resolution, allowing untrusted XML input to trigger external entity loading.
The factory instances lack security attributes to block external DTD and stylesheet access, leading to improper restriction of XML external entity references.

nodes.summary: restrict external dtd and stylesheet access
nodes.details: The patch explicitly sets the ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD and ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET attributes to empty strings on the factory instances to prevent external resource resolution.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The data loading routine processes user-supplied XML files for plot data visualization.
Attackers can provide arbitrary XML files through the build step configuration.
The XPath evaluation uses a default parser that does not disable external entity resolution, allowing XXE exploitation.
The patch replaces the direct input source with a utility method that configures the parser to disable external entity resolution.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered within the archive extraction method when processing individual entries into a destination directory.
The extraction process encounters an archive entry whose name matches a pre-existing symbolic link in the destination directory that points to a missing target.

Canonical path resolution returns the symbolic link's location instead of its target when the target is absent, causing the directory containment verification to pass while subsequent write operations follow the link to create files outside the intended directory.
The patch introduces a validation step to detect if the resolved destination path is a symbolic link and immediately rejects the extraction to prevent standard file writes from overriding it.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the addressing interceptor processes out-of-band replies or faults using destinations from request headers.
WS-Addressing must be configured with non-anonymous ReplyTo or FaultTo addresses in incoming SOAP requests.
The framework directly uses destination URIs from request headers to initiate outbound connections without verifying their safety or origin.
The patch introduces a source type parameter to distinguish remote from application-controlled destinations, enabling destination policy checks for remote addresses.
The vulnerability is triggered when the scanner plugin build step runs, affecting how Jenkins serves static files.
The plugin modifies a global system property to change the default Content-Security-Policy header for static files, impacting instances without a Resource Root URL.
Disabling the Content-Security-Policy header removes browser-enforced restrictions, allowing cross-site scripting attacks via controlled workspace or artifact files.
The patch removes the system property assignment, ensuring Jenkins retains its default Content-Security-Policy configuration for static file serving.
The vulnerability is triggered when processing XML messages through an XPath based selector during the dequeue operation.
Remote consumers can supply malicious XML payloads containing external entity references that are processed by the application.
The document builder factory is instantiated without disabling external entity resolution or restricting DOCTYPE declarations, allowing XXE exploitation.
The update configures the parser factory to disable external general and parameter entities, disallow DOCTYPE declarations, and ignore comments to mitigate XXE risks.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during the resolution of index patterns for fine-grained access control rules applied to data streams.
The issue requires an authenticated user who is authorized to read the targeted data streams to trigger the incorrect access authorization.
The index pattern resolution logic filters only aliases and excludes data streams, causing fine-grained access control rules to be incorrectly applied or bypassed for data stream backing indices.
The patch updates the index pattern resolution to filter for both aliases and data streams, and passes an includeDataStreams flag to the resolver to ensure correct access control application.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Information Exposure Through an External Information Bank

nodes.details: The application processes user-submitted attachments via a multipart form request and writes them to a local directory.
The system accepts a user-supplied filename from the upload request and uses it directly to determine the target file path on disk.
The validation logic only rejected filenames that exactly matched the traversal sequence, allowing sequences embedded within the string to bypass the check.
The patch updates the validation logic to detect the traversal sequence anywhere within the filename string, blocking directory traversal attempts.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The method processes input streams to skip whitespace and handle comment delimiters during tokenization.
The vulnerability triggers when the parser encounters a block comment that lacks a proper closing delimiter.
The loop iterating through comment characters fails to verify if the input stream has been exhausted before attempting to read the next character, leading to improper handling of unclosed comments.
The patch introduces a check to detect when no more characters are available, returning a null character to safely terminate parsing instead of causing undefined behavior.
The method extracts job parameter descriptions and formats them for display in the Jenkins interface.
Parameter descriptions are directly concatenated into HTML strings without sanitization, allowing malicious content to be stored.
User-supplied parameter values are rendered directly as HTML without neutralizing special characters, enabling stored cross-site scripting.
The update modifies the data structure to return a list and ensures parameter values are properly escaped before rendering to prevent XSS.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when resetting bean introspectors in the utility class, which determines which properties are accessible during reflection-based property access.
Applications pass external property paths directly to property access methods, allowing reflection to traverse enum objects and expose internal classloader references.
The default introspector configuration failed to suppress the declared class property on enum objects, leaving it accessible for unauthorized classloader retrieval.
The patch adds a new suppressor to the default introspector list, explicitly blocking access to the declared class property during bean introspection.
The vulnerability is triggered when the plugin initializes job configuration and stores the NuGet API key.
The plugin version prior to 2.0.5 stores the NuGet API key as a plain string in job configuration files without encryption.
The API key is stored and processed as a plain string instead of a protected secret type, and argument masking logic fails to cover it.
The patch changes the API key field to a secret type, retrieves plaintext only when necessary, and extends argument masking to include the API key parameter.
The method handles HTTP requests for validating repository connection settings and returns HTML-formatted responses to the user interface.
An exception is thrown during the validation of the repository URL, triggering the error handling block that constructs the response message.
The raw exception details are directly concatenated into an HTML string without sanitization, allowing malicious payloads within the error message to execute in the browser.
The patch wraps the exception output in an escaping utility to convert special HTML characters into safe entities before embedding the message in the response.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

nodes.details: This method constructs the Git checkout URI template and handles credential injection for repository access.
The issue manifests when the system is configured to use a personal access token for authenticating repository checkouts.
The implementation directly embeds the plain text token into the generated URI template without applying any masking or redaction mechanisms.
The patch removes the code block that constructs a URI containing the plain text token, preventing it from being exposed in generated templates or logs.
The method converts database parameter values into SQL string representations for query execution.
The vulnerability only occurs when the unsupported preferQueryMode connection property is explicitly set to simple.
The original conditional logic failed to handle several parameter types, causing them to be cast without proper type qualification and escaping.
The patch replaces the incomplete conditional chain with a switch statement that explicitly maps all supported parameter OIDs to their correct SQL type strings.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the S3EC is configured to store the encrypted data key in a separate instruction file instead of object metadata.
The system must be configured to use instruction files for storing the encrypted data key, which exposes the key to external modification.
The encryption implementation does not cryptographically bind the encrypted data key to the ciphertext, allowing an attacker to replace the key and decrypt to a different plaintext.
The patch introduces key commitment mechanisms to bind the encrypted data key to the ciphertext and updates metadata handling to enforce this cryptographic binding.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

nodes.details: The method processes user-supplied server credentials and configuration to test connectivity, serving as the attack surface for forged requests.
The endpoint accepts HTTP GET requests without verifying the request origin or method, allowing external sites to trigger it.
The validation function does not enforce POST-only submission, enabling attackers to exploit browser session cookies to execute unintended actions.
The patch applies a request method restriction annotation to the validation function, ensuring it only processes legitimate POST requests.
The vulnerability is triggered when the Jenkins Mercurial plugin processes an XML changelog file.
An attacker must be able to control an agent process or supply a crafted changelog file to the Jenkins controller.
The XML changelog parser was not configured to disable external entity resolution, enabling XXE attacks.
The update configures the XML parser to disable external entity resolution to prevent XXE exploitation.
The method processes user-supplied Groovy scripts via an HTTP request for form validation.
An attacker possessing Overall or Read permissions can submit malicious scripts to the endpoint.
The script parser is initialized without a secure compiler configuration, allowing execution of arbitrary code outside the sandbox.
The patch restricts the endpoint to POST requests and applies a secure compiler configuration to enforce sandbox restrictions during script parsing.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Use of Protection Mechanism that is not used or not implemented

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during the parsing of untrusted ciphertext headers.
An attacker provides encoded data containing a header field with an excessively large nonce length value.
The decoding logic directly uses the untrusted header value to allocate a byte array without size constraints.
The patch replaces direct decoding with a versioned header format and a dedicated parsing function that enforces strict size validation.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

nodes.details: The getToolTip method serves as the entrypoint that constructs and returns the tooltip content for job columns.
Users with Job or Configure permission can store arbitrary content in the job description field, which is later retrieved for display.
The method directly appends the raw job description string to the tooltip output without applying any formatting or escaping, enabling script injection.
The patch routes the job description through the configured markup formatter translate method before appending it to the tooltip output.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: Attackers exploit the asType method in the ScriptBytecodeAdapter class to bypass the sandbox whitelist and invoke arbitrary constructors in sandboxed scripts.
The vulnerability occurs when sandboxed Jenkins Pipeline scripts execute Groovy type coercion operations that trigger the permitsStaticMethod whitelist check.
The whitelist unconditionally returns true for ScriptBytecodeAdapter.asType calls without verifying if the target type or object is safe, enabling arbitrary constructor invocation.
The patch modifies the whitelist to call Checker.preCheckedCast for asType operations, ensuring that type coercions are validated against sandbox rules before being permitted.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code

nodes.details: The vulnerability is accessed through a filter extension point that selectively disables cross-site request forgery protection for specific request paths.
The implementation incorrectly exempts any request path matching a specific suffix pattern from CSRF validation, allowing arbitrary target URLs to bypass protection.
The filter condition uses a suffix match for a proxy endpoint, which inadvertently grants CSRF exemption to any URL containing that suffix, enabling attackers to bypass protection.
The patch removes the suffix matching condition, restricting the CSRF exemption strictly to the intended callback URL and requiring the JavaScript component to pass the CSRF token.
The vulnerability is triggered during the source control configuration phase when the system initializes the Git client builder.
The original implementation passes credential identifiers directly to the client builder constructor during the build process.
Embedding credentials directly in the builder configuration causes the access token to be formatted into the repository URL, which is subsequently written to build logs.
The patch replaces direct credential passing with a dedicated authentication extension to prevent token leakage into loggable URLs.
The vulnerability is triggered within the function composition layer when processing requests that involve chained function execution.
The issue requires a scenario where a function is explicitly composed with itself using the composition API without prior validation.
The composition method lacks a guard against self-referential composition, leading to infinite recursion that exhausts system memory during request handling.
The patch introduces a validation check to detect when a function is composed with itself, immediately throwing an exception to halt recursive execution.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Unnecessary Action in Always Executed Code Block

nodes.details: The method in TestObject.java responsible for updating test result descriptions.
Exploitation requires the victim to have an active authenticated session with the Jenkins instance.
The endpoint accepted state-changing requests without enforcing the POST method or unconditionally verifying user permissions.
The patch introduces a POST requirement annotation and relocates the permission validation outside conditional logic to block forged requests.
The vulnerability is triggered when job configurations containing sensitive credentials are persisted to the Jenkins controller's storage.
Prior to the fix, the plugin stored sensitive API keys and passwords as plain text strings directly in configuration files without encryption.
The plugin's data binding and file writing mechanisms directly serialized password fields as unencrypted strings, exposing them to users with read access or filesystem privileges.
The patch modifies credential fields to use a secure wrapper type, ensuring passwords are encrypted upon serialization and securely decrypted only when accessed programmatically.
Processes the authentication callback request to establish user sessions.
An existing session is present when the authentication callback is invoked.
The authentication flow retains the original session identifier instead of generating a new one after successful login.
The update explicitly invalidates the existing session and creates a fresh one upon successful authentication.
The plugin stores webhook URLs containing secret tokens in global and job configuration files on the Jenkins master.
Webhook URLs and secret tokens are persisted in plaintext within configuration files accessible to users with extended read permissions.
The endpoint configuration field was implemented as a standard String type, causing sensitive webhook URLs to be saved without encryption.
The patch changes the endpoint field type from String to Secret, ensuring credentials are encrypted upon storage and securely decrypted during retrieval.
The vulnerability is triggered within the PostgreSQL JDBC driver's result set processing when handling query parameters.
The attack requires the driver to be explicitly configured with PreferQueryMode=SIMPLE, as the default mode prevents exploitation.
Improper validation of adjacent numeric and string placeholders allows an attacker to construct payloads that bypass parameterized query protections and inject SQL.
The patch introduces null checks, explicit OID type verification, and safe string comparisons to prevent unexpected data handling and ensure robust type processing.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command (SQL Injection)

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered within the security manager's permission checking logic when evaluating thread-based access requests.
The security manager previously granted unconditional permission bypass to any operation executed on the Java Event Dispatch Thread.
Remote attackers leverage this unconditional bypass by routing malicious robot code through SwingUtilities.invokeLater to execute arbitrary Java code with elevated privileges.
The update restricts the thread bypass by validating the call stack to ensure requests originate exclusively from authorized internal utility classes.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered through the Windows Remote Command library used to execute remote commands for Java version checking and installation.
Users must be able to connect to a named pipe to trigger the remote command execution capability provided by the plugin.
The Windows Remote Command library contains a buffer overflow vulnerability that allows arbitrary command execution when processing remote requests.
The patch removes the code block that invokes the Windows Remote Command library for automatic Java detection and installation.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Buffer

nodes.details: Test initialization method configuring OIDC provider metadata and client credentials for validation testing.
The OpenID Connect provider permits the none algorithm, which allows tokens to be issued without cryptographic signatures.
The validation mechanism fails to explicitly refuse unsigned tokens, enabling attackers to bypass verification by injecting malformed tokens with an empty signature.
Update the mocked configuration to reference the correct secret variable, ensuring the test setup accurately reflects expected credential handling.
The vulnerability is triggered when the evaluateCriteria method processes database-stored criteria strings.
An attacker possessing the Manage Concepts privilege can inject malicious template expressions into concept reference range fields.
The method evaluates user-supplied strings using an Apache Velocity engine without sandboxing, enabling unrestricted Java reflection.
The patch removes the Apache Velocity evaluation logic and substitutes it with a safer expression language parser to prevent code injection.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the write endpoint for predicted datapoints processes requests, incorrectly granting modification capabilities to unauthorized users.
The vulnerability requires a user to possess only read asset permissions while attempting to access the write endpoint for predicted datapoints.
The implementation incorrectly validates the read asset role instead of a write-specific role during the write operation, allowing unauthorized data modification.
The patch replaces the read role validation with a write-specific role check and updates metadata attribute verification to enforce proper write permissions.
The vulnerability occurs during the parsing of CBOR binary values where the declared length exceeds the actual available input data.
A CBOR document specifies a binary value length that is larger than the number of bytes actually present in the input stream.
The parser allocates a byte array matching the declared length immediately without verifying if the input stream contains sufficient data, causing excessive memory consumption.
The patch replaces unconditional buffer allocation with explicit end-of-input checks, ensuring an error is thrown if insufficient data is available before memory is allocated.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

nodes.details: The REST API endpoints for retrieving user profiles and roles accept a realm parameter but lack proper realm boundary validation, allowing cross-tenant enumeration.
The vulnerability requires an attacker to possess valid authentication credentials and the administrative read role within a non-master tenant realm.
The affected read methods validate the caller's administrative role but fail to verify that the target user's realm matches the caller's authenticated realm, allowing cross-realm data retrieval.
The patch introduces a validation guard at the start of the affected methods to ensure the target user belongs to the caller's authenticated realm before proceeding.
The vulnerability is triggered during the bundle upload process when error messages from server responses or internal exceptions are processed and displayed.
The plugin directly processes and displays responses from the external advisory server or internal exceptions without prior sanitization.
Raw error messages and server responses are directly embedded into HTML-formatted error strings without escaping, allowing malicious payloads to execute.
